column36: Does pre-gestational type 1 or type 2 diabetes lower omega-3 fatty acids in the cord blood of new borns and thus interfere with neurodevelopment?
column37: Docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) is a long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acid that is essential for healthy brain and nervous system development during pregnancy. During the third trimester, maternal lipolytic activity is increased in order to meet the fetus's increased need for DHA. A deficiency in DHA at this time could be detrimental to the neurodevelopment of the fetus. Previous studies have shown that pregnant women with type 1 or type 2 diabetes (T1D or T2D), also known as pre-gestational diabetes (PGD), have lower levels of DHA in their red blood cells. It has also been observed that in diabetic pregnancies, less DHA is present in the umbilical cord blood compared to non-diabetic pregnancies and that DHA may be accumulated in the placenta instead of being released into the cord blood. In this project, we will explore the link between fatty acids in newborns and T1D and T2D mothers and neurological measurements in the babies. We hypothesize that PGD mothers have a placental defect that alters the transfer of DHA to the cord blood and this will result in lower neurodevelopment of the occipital brain region. We also hypothesize that the neurodevelopment of the newborn is positively correlated with DHA concentrations in the cord blood. We will evaluate the fatty acid profile of maternal plasma, cord blood, and the placenta using gas chromatography. Moreover, we will assess the expression of various placental fatty acid transporters using Western Blot and mass spectrometry. Finally, we will evaluate the neurodevelopment of the newborns using electroencephalography (EEG) 24-48 hours after birth and at 2 months of age. The results of this project will help us to better understand the impact that PGD may have on the fatty acid status and the neurodevelopment of newborns.

column36: Weight Status and Lower Academic Acheivement for Canadian Adolescents with Obesity
column37: My research will examine the relationship between weight status and academic achievement in Canadian youth with obesity. My interest in weight bias, or the prejudice and discrimination that people with obesity encounter in health care and employment settings led me to question what impact, if any, does weight bias have on students with obesity in the school environment; and whether it can explain lower grades? Few studies examined the relationship between weight status and academic performance for youth with obesity and they show a connection between increased weight and lower academic performance. The reasons for this correlation are not yet clear. We know from weight bias literature that some physical education teacher hold biased beliefs about students with obesity. My thesis will focus on examining if low self-concept, potentially because of the negative impact of weight bias, can explain why youth with obesity perform lower than their average weight peers. I plan on doing this using quantitative statistics from a large sample of Canadian secondary school students using the COMPASS study data. This is an important relationship to examine because lower academic achievement can set a lifelong trajectory into adulthood for young people. Lower grades are associated with less pursuit of post-secondary education and higher chances of unemployment, poverty and poor health. The findings can impact millions of Canadian children and youth since an estimated third or more of Canadian children/youth are at risk of obesity. Findings can also be used to inform public health programing in an attempt to implement early intervention programs in primary school settings and foster non-biased environments in school for students and staff.

column36: Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) for Breast Cancer Patients undergoing Autologous Microvascular Breast Reconstruction
column37: Breast cancer affects 1 in 8 Canadian women. While treatments for breast cancer have improved survival to 87%, studies show that women who undergo mastectomy often experience a negative impact to their quality of life. Breast reconstruction benefits patients by improving their physical, psychosocial and sexual well-being. Patients who undergo breast reconstruction have the choice between alloplastic (implant-based) or autologous (tissue-based). Although implant-based reconstruction is the most common form of breast reconstruction in North America, autologous reconstruction using the patient's own skin, fat and muscle has superior long-term patient satisfaction. The current standard for autologous reconstruction is the DIEP (deep inferior epigastric perforator) flap, using the patient's abdominal tissue to reconstruct the breast using microsurgical techniques. However, DIEP reconstruction is a longer and more complex operation involving surgery at the breasts and abdominal donor-site. This results in longer hospital stays and increased opioid use for pain control compared to implant-based reconstruction. Enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) is a multidisciplinary approach to patient care before, during, and after surgery that has improved recovery for patients that undergo colorectal surgery. Patients who are in the ERAS pathway are able to return home earlier following surgery, with better pain control and less opioid use. The principles of ERAS can be transferred for patients undergoing autologous breast reconstruction. The proposed research is to implement ERAS for breast cancer patients undergoing DIEP breast reconstruction and understand its impact on patient recovery. The results have the potential to improve patient care and reduce healthcare costs.

column36: Identification of a novel compound that reduces mortality from severe influenza and elucidation of its molecular mechanisms
column37: The influenza virus causes hundreds of thousands of deaths annually worldwide. There is a constant threat of a novel strain developing, leading to an influenza pandemic. While antivirals exist for the treatment of infections, the virus changes quickly and cases of resistance to these drugs have already occurred. As such, novel therapeutics for the treatment of influenza are urgently needed. Recent findings have shown that the host body's response to infection can be damaging and cause death. Consequently, drugs that alter the body's response to the virus, instead of directly targeting the virus, may be useful for the treatment of influenza. We have identified a drug that protects both zebrafish and mice from death due to influenza infection. So far, our studies show that the drug does not seem to repress the virus itself, which means it should not lead to viral resistance. Rather, it seems that the drug is improving how the body responds to the virus. This project is designed to figure out specifically how the drug works at the level of cells and molecules, so it can be developed to use for the treatment of influenza patients. To do this, we will use sophisticated molecular biology techniques and computer-aided analysis to identify the target of the drug.

column36: The liver-x-receptor/endothelial progenitor cell secretome: a new source of anti-atherogenic proteins
column37: Heart disease is the leading cause of death worldwide, representing 31% of annual mortalities. A major contributing factor to heart disease is atherosclerosis, the hardening of arteries due to plaque buildup. Atherosclerosis begins when endothelial cells lining the artery become physically or chemically damaged. This induces endothelial dysfunction, which allows the accumulation of cholesterol and inflammatory cells within the arteries, leading to plaque formation. Cholesterol-rich plaques can rupture, creating blood clots that can cause a heart attack or stroke. Currently, the prevention of atherosclerosis is managed by statin drugs that reduce blood cholesterol levels. However, since cholesterol reduction does not fully prevent vascular complications, novel therapies targeting early atherosclerosis are urgently needed. The proposed project will study bone-marrow derived endothelial progenitor cells (EPCs) and investigate how enhancing EPC function can repair and protect endothelial cells during early atherosclerosis. Previous studies have shown that the activation of a nuclear protein, liver X receptor (LXR), reduces intracellular cholesterol levels in macrophages, a primary atherosclerotic inflammatory cell type. Interestingly, our lab recently found that LXR activation in murine EPCs causes these stem-like cells to secrete protective factors to decrease early plaque formation. We aim to reveal how LXRs interact with EPCs to elicit their protective role, identify which secreted factors contribute to the observed effects and determine its reproducibility in human EPCs. This project will enhance our understanding of the fundamental mechanisms by which EPCs support damaged endothelial cells during early atherogenesis, and identify potential new therapeutic targets.

column36: Evaluating the impact of public policies on responses to drug overdoses among people who use illicit drugs (PWUD) in Vancouver, Canada
column37: Canada has been experiencing an opioid overdose crisis in the past few years. The first and most critical response to an overdose event is to call 911 for help. Despite this, many people who use illicit drugs (PWUD) do not call 911 at the scene of an overdose because of fear towards the police. In response, two key policies have emerged in hopes to encourage PWUD to call for emergency help. In 2005, the Vancouver Police Department (VPD) adopted a non-attendance policy, which means that the police will not attend overdose events unless a death has occurred or if the BC Emergency Health Services request for their attendance. Similarly, in 2017, a federal law known as the Good Samaritan Drug Overdose Act (GSA) was introduced. This law provides legal protection from simple drug possession charges to any person who calls for help at the scene of an overdose. However, for various reasons, it is unclear whether the GSA or VPD's non-attendance policy have been successful in increasing the amount of calls to 911 at the event of an overdose. The effectiveness of these policies may determine whether PWUD call for emergency help, which reduces the chance an overdose becomes fatal. This proposal will evaluate the effectiveness and the impact of both policies using a large study that consists of over 3,000 PWUD. Information regarding police attendance and overdose response have been collected since 2004. Currently, no research has evaluated the effectiveness of these policies and little is known about PWUD's responses to overdose events in Canada. Therefore, this study will fill an important knowledge gap in the scientific community that will help inform the current policies, as well as future policies, aimed to encourage PWUD to call for emergency help at the scene of an overdose.

column36: The role of community-based social networks in facilitating healthcare access and use among low income individuals: a qualitative study in Negros Occidental, Philippines
column37: Despite impressive economic growth and efforts to expand universal healthcare coverage, disparities in healthcare access and quality remain across the Philippines, with low income individuals continuing to experience barriers to healthcare access. Community-based social networks (i.e., relationships between households within and between communities) may be fundamental for sharing information about healthcare access and use, which may increase awareness and access to care among low income individuals. Sampling will be purposive to allow for a broad cross section of backgrounds and experiences to be included in the study. I will thematically analyze the interviews and share the findings with ICM to inform the organization's ongoing efforts to improve access and use of healthcare services among income poor individuals.

column36: Role des proteases dans la Dystrophie endotheliale corneenne de Fuchs
column37: Toutes maladies de l'oeil causent des pertes de vision et peuvent meme mener a la cecite. C'est le cas d'une maladie de l'oeil qui affecte la cornee (la partie transparente a l'avant de l'oeil) appelee << Dystrophie endotheliale corneenne de Fuchs >>. Cette maladie touche 4% de la population et est responsable de 17 000 greffes de cornee annuellement en Amerique du nord. Le premier signe clinique de cette maladie est l'epaississement d'une membrane, causee par l'accumulation de proteines matricielles. Or, le corps humain possede des enzymes qui sont responsables de la regulation des proteines matricielles, soit des proteases. Nous suggerons qu'une deregulation de ces proteases dans l'oeil serait responsable de l'epaississement de la membrane retrouvee dans la Dystrophie endotheliale corneenne de Fuchs. L'objectif de ce projet est donc d'analyser le profil de proteases produites par les cellules de la cornee. Pour ce faire, notre laboratoire utilise les cellules de la cornee qui ont ete isolees et mises en culture pour permettre leur etude dans des conditions controlees. Nous allons ensuite valider l'importance de cette deregulation de proteases dans le developpement de la maladie. Ce projet permettra une meilleure comprehension de l'etape charniere de la Dystrophie endotheliale corneenne de Fuchs, soit de l'accumulation excessive de proteines matricielles. De plus, l'identification d'une diminution des proteases pourrait mener au developpement de nouvelles avenues therapeutiques specifiques, visant par exemple la degradation partielle de la membrane, ce qui eviterait la perte de vision et le recours aux greffes.

column37: Diabetes results from the destruction of insulin-producing ?-cells in pancreatic islets of Langerhans, leaving patients unable to control blood glucose. column37: The proposed study seeks to use the automated spatial memory improvement program (auto-SMIP) to alleviate memory deficits associated with dysfunction of the hippocampus (HPC) in patients with traumatic brain injury (TBI). Both healthy and TBI patients will undergo 16 hours of auto-SMIP intervention over 8 weeks. Both groups are expected to show cognitive improvements related to the HPC and MRI differences at post-test and at the 6-month follow-up. Differences between these groups will also demonstrate auto-SMIP to be an effective intervention in protecting against hippocampal atrophy, thereby preserving associated cognitive functions. The micro-vascularization of the HPC, which shares networks with many other key brain areas, makes it particularly susceptible to TBI-related atrophy. Further to HPC-related memory deficits, secondary damage resulting from neuronal hyperexcitation have lead to functional disturbances related to mood disorders and prolonged decrease in quality of life for TBI patients. Nevertheless, previous research suggest that interventions promoting cognitive activity may significantly moderate recovery outcomes. Specifically, HPC-dependent spatial memory strategies have been associated with improved cognition and greater HPC activity compared to non-HPC dependent compensatory strategies. In a recent study, the 8-week auto-SMIP intervention was found to induce HPC growth in older adults with reduced HPC, maintained over 6 months, which the current study proposes to demonstrate in TBI patients. To date, auto-SMIP is the only cognitive intervention that has demonstrated targeted improvements specific to the HPC. As such the current study will demonstrate auto-SMIP training effects such as enhanced spatial memory and improved quality of life.

column36: Inhibition of hypoxia-inducible metastasis promoting gene transcription
column37: Despite the improvement of therapeutics for cancer, it is still the leading cause of death in North America. Cancers become more fatal once they spread to organs which are essential for survival. Undoubtedly, a better strategy which will selectively target and prevent the spreading of cancers is needed. It has been shown that cancers which form solid tumours outgrow their oxygen-rich blood supply and develop a response to survive under a low oxygen environment (hypoxia). This low oxygen driven response not only allows tumour cells to survive under hypoxia but also transforms the cells to become more invasive (metastatic) and aggressive. This survival response is only activated in the tumour cells and not healthy cells. Thus, targeting the mechanism of the survival response is a novel strategy to prevent cancer metastasis which can lead to more effective therapeutics. Our hypothesis is that if the mechanism of the survival response is disrupted, this will stop tumour cells from spreading. I will first characterize this mechanism using highly sensitive biochemical techniques. I will then screen for small molecules that disrupt this survival response. As metastatic cancer accounts for the majority of cancer-related deaths, and the currently available treatments, such as radiotherapy and chemotherapy, cannot effectively target metastatic cancers and instead affect healthy cells, this research will provide helpful information for better therapeutics. The insight I may gain from this research will be useful to all cancer types which form solid tumours such as prostate and breast cancers, the most commonly diagnosed cancers in Canadian males and females, respectively.

column36: Closing the Northern Gap: Stakeholder Perspectives on an eHealth App for Maternal Mental Health in Northwestern Ontario
column37: Women living in Northwestern Ontario (NWO) face many unique barriers in accessing healthcare when compared to those living outside of the North. Peri- and Postpartum depression affects women almost twice as much as men, suicide is the leading cause of death among pregnant women, and hospitalizations for mental health and self-injury in NWO are double the national rate. Yet, There is still a significant gap in access to maternal care and mental health services in NWO. This study will address this gap by exploring the suitability of an eHealth intervention for mothers with peri- and postnatal depression. Therapist-Assisted Internet-delivered Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (TA-ICBT) is an eHealth tool that can be used as a mobile 'app' to match patients with trained therapists, provide online self-management videos, and recommend services to best meet patients' needs. Because TA-ICBT can be delivered remotely, it has the potential to overcome many of the common barriers faced by women in the North. Twenty interviews and four focus groups will be conducted in order to understand what physicians, nurses, and other care providers perceive as key barriers and enablers to using a TA-ICBT app in NWO. This information will be used to adapt the app to best serve our target population. This research will be overseen by an interdisciplinary team of women who have been collecting data on the maternal health in NWO over the past five years. The aim of this study is to inform the future design, development, and delivery of a new TA-ICBT app for women in NWO. This research will be a foundation from which a new healthcare option can be developed to meet the specific needs of women in NWO, and will help close the Northern gap in maternal mental health services.

column36: The influence of apolipoprotein E4 on microglial activity in cervical spondylotic myelopathy
column37: Cervical spondylotic myelopathy (CSM) is a devastating neurological condition resulting from the degeneration of spinal structures and the subsequent compression of the spinal cord. CSM is the most common cause of spinal cord dysfunction among adults (>55 years), and can result in severe sensory and motor deficits. Individuals carrying the apolipoprotein E4 (ApoE4) allele have a 77.8% greater risk of developing CSM, and have worse neurological outcomes following surgical treatment. While the role of ApoE4 in CSM pathology is currently unknown, recent evidence suggests that ApoE acts as a ligand for a crucial microglial receptor complex: Triggering Receptor Expressed on Myeloid Cells 2 (TREM2) and DNAX-activating protein 12 (DAP12). Microglia are the innate immune cells of the central nervous system, and inflammatory activation of microglia results in the release of nitric oxide, cytokines, and proteases that can lead to neurotoxicity. Given that activated microglia are known to participate in CSM spinal cord pathology, I hypothesize that the ApoE4 isoform exacerbates CSM progression by promoting a pro-inflammatory microglial phenotype, specifically through interaction with the TREM2-DAP12 complex. The proposed study will focus on the following goals: (1) investigate the neuroinflammatory role ApoE4 and the TREM2-DAP12 complex has on CSM and (2) determine whether inhibition of TREM2-DAP12 signaling can mitigate the negative effect of ApoE4 on the complex in the diseased state. This proposal is the first to investigate the role of ApoE4 in CSM neuroinflammatory mechanisms and experimentally link ApoE4 expression to neurological outcomes in CSM. It will also provide proof-of-concept for a novel personalized medicine strategy to treat an at-risk ApoE4+ CSM population.

column36: Individual Level Prediction of Cognitive Decline in Alzheimer's Disease
column37: Alzheimer's Disease (AD) is a devastating neurodegenerative disease with an immense burden on society. A 2017 estimate showed that AD affects over 5 million individuals in the U.S. alone and costs over $200 billions. While no cure has been found, early-detection of AD help with in early-intervention which improves the patients' quality of life and reduces the cost to society. For this reason, individual-level prediction of AD is essential. As it stands, current AD research has identified numerous group-level differences between AD and non-AD subjects, but no robust subject-level detection system is available. This is the problem I would like to solve. Specifically, I will be attempting to predict the decline in cognitive abilities experienced by patients suffering from AD, using machine learning methodologies. I will use unsupervised clustering to identify groups of patients who has similar cognitive trajectories across time (e.g. one group may maintain a high degree of cognitive abilities as they age, while another may show rapid decline). Importantly, I will be extending upon previous works done in the lab to include many different clinical rating scales to provide a nuanced measure of each individual's cognitive ability. Then, I will borrow methods from supervised machine learning to predict which trajectory each subject belongs to, using data that can be collected in the clinic, such as demography, genetics and neuroanatomical structures. This work holds the promise of constructing a robust predictive algorithm which can help clinicians be more informed and make better clinical decisions with regard to the treatment of AD patients.

column36: An aggregate algorithmic approach to prioritizing HIV-1 transmission clusters
column37: For the 37 million people infected with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), treatment can increase length and quality of life, and prevent transmission to uninfected people. However, over 40% of infected people do not have access to treatment and 1.8 million infections still occur each year. Making sure public health resources can quickly reach people with HIV is important in helping them get treatment that will let them live longer, better lives and prevent the spread of infection. Right now, public health agencies can use HIV DNA samples collected from infected people to identify groups that are transmitting HIV at a high rate. However, this type of approach does not define which group of people needs public health attention most. Adding medical and personal information about the people in high-transmission groups to this method could help determine which group needs targeted attention. Current methods also do not use information about the uninfected people who interact with the people in high-transmission groups, even though their characteristics may affect the rate of HIV transmission. I propose to develop a new method that will identify groups of people who are transmitting HIV at a high rate and determine which of these groups needs public health attention most. First, I will establish an improved method of identifying high-transmission groups based on HIV DNA samples. Next, I will create a computer algorithm that will combine medical and personal information from the people in high-transmission groups together with personal information from the uninfected people they interact with. The algorithm will calculate a score that will rank high-transmission groups by need for public health resources, so that these resources can be used in the best way possible.

column36: Long-term Care Facilities: Ownership Status and Patient Self-Reported Outcomes
column37: Residential care facilities provide 24-hour supervision, care and accommodation to individuals with complex care needs who can no longer live safely at home. The goal of the proposed research is examine differences in self-reported patient views of health across residential care facilities in B.C. We will then assess the relationship between this variation and both facility ownership characteristics and facility-level quality outcomes. Overall, we anticipate that there will be strong correlations between patient views and other measures of facility structure and performance. More specifically, we hypothesize: 1) self-reported patient outcomes will be more homogeneous within a facility than between facilities; 2) self-reported patient outcomes will differ significantly based on the ownership status of the facility, with health authority-owned and non-profit facilities having better patient-reported outcomes than for-profit facilities; and 3) there will be a similar relationship between patient-reported outcomes and quality outcomes. These data are linkable to other information including facility characteristics (e.g. size, ownership and profit status) and patient information that are part of the Resident Assessment Instrument (RAI) data. We will first perform descriptive analyses of the data. Because individual residents are nested within facilities, we will use hierarchical linear modelling to explain the within-facility and between-facility variation in patient self-reported outcomes.

column36: Remote Ischemic Post-Conditioning in Patients with Traumatic Brain Injury: A Prospective Randomized Control Trial
column37: Traumatic brain injury (TBI), an impact to the brain caused by an external force, is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in victims of blunt trauma. In 2010, Statistics Canada reported that 133,812 people had sustained a brain injury in the household population. Additionally, incidence numbers are projected to increase by 28% over the next 20 years, according to a 2014 Public Health Agency of Canada report. Due to the complexity introduced by TBI, many conventional approaches fall short. Currently, the management of TBI largely focuses on prevention or reduction of secondary consequences which occur hours to days later from the initial trauma and play a major role in a poor prognosis, which may entail long-term cognitive impairment. To counteract this, it is crucial to support brain circulation, reduce intracranial (i.e. within the skull) fluid retention, and/or decrease metabolic activity during periods of elevated intracranial pressure. Thus, we propose using the low-cost non-invasive Remote Ischemic Conditioning (RIC) procedure. RIC is inducing brief periods of restricted blood flow via a blood pressure cuff at a limb. RIC then elicits inborn systemic protection in distant organs, hence, minimizing subsequent trauma. Research in RIC has shown its benefits to other organs such as the heart and kidneys and at a molecular level in TBI. In this human study, we plan to examine RIC benefits in severe TBI patients by measuring several factors such as brain inflammation markers, brain circulation via imaging technology, and finally, overall cognitive improvement. The implementation of this simple procedure may significantly improve TBI patient outcome and we hope the findings of this study will promote RIC research in other neurological conditions.

column36: The effects of exercise and inflammation on neuropathic pain in individuals with a spinal cord injury.
column37: Neuropathic pain (NP) is self-reported as the most severe type of pain following a traumatic spinal cord injury (SCI) and places the largest burden on the healthcare system compared to all other types of pain. Although most treatment options for NP are pharmaceutical interventions, this line of treatment only addresses the symptoms rather than the cause of NP. Promising research has shown that exercise can also reduce NP although the mechanism by which this occurs is unknown. One proposed explanation is that exercise reduces inflammation which in turn reduces NP. Under normal circumstances, the inflammatory response is a healthy way for the body to be made aware of acute injurious stimuli and respond accordingly. However, in individuals with SCI, evidence suggests that nervous system impairments can lead to the dysregulation of both endocrine and immune function which can lead to a chronic low-grade inflammation. This chronic low-grade inflammation has been linked to a variety of negative health problems. This study attempts to use exercise to reduce inflammation in people with SCI to reduce NP. Participants will complete a 12-week exercise trial consisting of 20 to 30-minutes of moderate to vigorous physical activity 3 times a week in accordance with SCI specific exercise guidelines. Blood samples will be taken to monitor the levels of inflammation in the blood and NP will be assessed using a validated subjective measure. This study will allow us to better understand how exercise can reduce NP in people with SCI and more specifically what role exercise plays in inflammation. This will allow clinicians, rehabilitation specialists, and other healthcare professionals to create better non-pharmaceutical interventions aimed to reduce inflammation and NP in people with SCI.

column37: Young people, especially young women, face disproportionate barriers to health and social services access. column36: Les effets d'une intervention d'ecoute musicale a domicile sur les symptomes depressifs des personnes atteintes de la maladie d'Alzheimer en debut d'evolution
column37: Compte tenu de l'avancement en age de la population, les previsions concernant la prevalence de maladies cognitives telles que la maladie d'Alzheimer sont a la hausse (Societe Alzheimer du Canada, 2016). Dans le but d'attenuer les symptomes ainsi que d'ameliorer la qualite de vie des patients atteints, de plus en plus de recherches se sont penches sur les bienfaits de la therapie musicale. Malgre un interet grandissant pour ce sujet, peu de recherches systematiques ont examine ses effets sur les symptomes depressifs vecus par les gens souffrant de cette maladie. Ce projet a donc pour objectif de contribuer a l'avancement des connaissances en mesurant les effets d'une intervention d'ecoute musicale personnalisee et realisee a domicile sur les symptomes depressifs de la maladie d'Alzheimer en debut d'evolution. 60 participants seront separes en deux groupes independants. Le premier groupe (controle) ecoutera des sons tires de l'environnement alors que le deuxieme groupe (experimental) sera expose a l'intervention musicale. Le tout se deroulera sur une periode de 6 semaines et chaque session sera d'une duree de 20 minutes. Il est prevu que l'ecoute musicale diminuera la presence de symptomes depressifs au cours des sessions et que ses effets seront plus significatifs que ceux de l'ecoute de sons dans l'environnement. L'intervention musicale a l'avantage d'etre non-invasive, peu couteuse et facile a integrer dans la vie des patients. Elle est une donc solution pratique pour les gens vivant encore a domicile et ses effets ont le potentiel d'etre benefiques en debut de maladie.

column36: Characterization of Molecular Partners of the Programmed Cell Death Protein 1/Programmed Death-ligand 1 Immune Checkpoint in Tumour Cells
column37: Immune checkpoints are vital regulators of the host immune system. They provide a balance between co-stimulators and inhibitors of immune cells, preventing over-stimulation that can otherwise lead to inflammation and auto-immunity. However, tumour cells can take advantage of this innate system as a way to deactivate immune cells and evade the host immune system, termed immune escape. Programmed Death 1 (PD-1) is one such immune checkpoint found on immune cells. It interacts with Programmed Death-Ligand 1 (PD-L1) on tumour cells and results in the deactivation of immune cells, conferring immune escape. Strategies have been developed to interfere with this PD-1/PD-L1 interaction, including drugs called immune checkpoint blockers. These immune checkpoint blockers have demonstrated exceptionally high response rates in patients with advanced stages of cancer, providing new promise. However, there are limitations to the current use of immune checkpoint blockers. For reasons not yet known, the majority of patients do not significantly benefit from this therapy, despite the high response rates. This demonstrates that there is still a lot to be known about the PD-1/PD-L1 axis. Quite recent research has elucidated that the PD-1/PD-L1 interaction not only affects immune cells, but also exerts a change on the tumour cells, causing them to exhibit a more malignant phenotype, including drug resistance and metastasis. Our proposed research aims to identify proteins within the tumour cells interacting with PD-L1 that facilitate malignant progression. This knowledge would provide us greater insight into the underpinnings of immune checkpoints, and could ultimately impact the timing of therapies as well as potentially elucidate new druggable targets.

column36: Target validation of ACLY as a novel anti-cancer drug target for hepatocellular carcinoma
column37: ATP citrate lyase (ACLY) performs an essential role in de novo lipogenesis by catalyzing the synthesis of cytosolic acetyl-CoA. De novo lipogenesis is upregulated in cancer in order to compensate for the metabolic demands of rapid cell proliferation. This is because lipid is an important macromolecule for cell proliferation due to its roles in membrane biogenesis, cell signaling and energy production/storage. Therefore, it is not surprising that ACLY is upregulated in various types of cancer and correlates with poor patient prognosis. However, the role of ACLY in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains largely unknown. Currently, the net 5 year survival rate of HCC is 19% and its incidence is rapidly increasing in Canada. Unfortunately, Sorafenib and Lenvatinib, the lone first-line standard of treatment drugs for HCC, could only extend median survival by 3 - 4 months. Thus, validation of ACLY as a novel drug target for HCC either alone or in combination with these drugs is of critical interest for improving the standard of care for HCC. The proposed study aims to discover and validate the role of ACLY in HCC through both pharmacological and genetic inhibition of ACLY activity.

column36: Utilite clinique des tests d'oscillometrie respiratoire en ajout a l'evaluation clinique de l'asthme chez les enfants d'age prescolaire
column37: L'asthme est une maladie respiratoire comportant deux sous-types caracterises par des symptomes persistants ou recurrents. Le principal test utilise pour diagnostiquer le sous-type d'asthme est appele spirometrie, ce qui necessite que les patients expirent avec force. Il est difficile d'identifier le sous-type d'asthme chez les enfants de moins de 6 ans, car la spirometrie n'est pas adaptee aux enfants de ce groupe d'age. De plus, il est difficile de se procurer des appareils de spirometrie dans la communaute, ou 85% des enfants asthmatiques sont traites. Une alternative interessante est un test appele l'oscillometrie (OS), qui exige que les enfants respirent normalement, un test plus adapte aux enfants de moins de 6 ans. A date, l'utilite de ce test pour suivre et ajuster le traitement d'enfants asthmatiques n'a pas ete formellement etudiee. Cette etude va evaluer l'utilite de l'OS pour identifier le sous-type d'asthme chez les enfants de moins de 6, ainsi que l'effet des tests reguliers d'OS sur les medicaments prescrits par les medecins pour controler les symptomes asthmatiques de leurs patients. Pour ce faire, les donnees de deux grandes bases de donnees fournie par les cliniques d'asthme de deux hopitaux pediatriques a Montreal seront utilisees. L'etude comparera les donnees d'enfants asthmatiques ages de moins de 6 ans appartenant a deux groupes distinct. Un groupe est constitue de 390 enfants qui ont subi des tests reguliers par OS, tandis que l'autre groupe est constitue de 811 enfants qui n'ont jamais subi de tests d'OS. Si les tests d'OS s'averent utiles, la commercialisation recente d'appareils d'OS portables ne necessitant aucun professionnel pour les operer, permettra aux medecins de la communaute de beneficier de l'utilisation de cette technique.

column36: Role of Eosinophils During Bacterial Infection
column37: Eosinophils are a type of immune cell that are present in the intestinal tract of healthy individuals. During inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) the number of intestinal eosinophils rises, and a higher number of eosinophils is associated with more severe disease. In addition, IBD leaves patients at higher risk of infection with harmful bacteria. The role of eosinophils in this context is unknown: are eosinophils helpful in contributing to a protective immune response against bacteria or is the presence of eosinophils allowing the bacteria to thrive in the intestinal tract? This research project aims to determine whether, and how, the presence of eosinophils alters the outcome of infection with a bacterial pathogen. I hypothesize that eosinophils promote intestinal colonization by bacterial pathogens. To test this hypothesis, I will orally infect wild-type and eosinophil-deficient mice with a model bacterial pathogen and track the resulting inflammation, pathology and bacterial burdens along the intestinal tract. The use of these mouse models will allow for the determination of causal relationships between eosinophils and susceptibility to bacterial pathogens. The Reynolds lab has state of the art research equipment in addition to all other necessary resources for the completion of this project. Canada has one of the highest rates of inflammatory bowel disease worldwide. To better treat and manage IBD it is necessary to understand how immune cell types such as eosinophils contribute to disease. As well as contributing to health knowledge, carrying out this research will allow me to acquire the necessary skills and techniques to continue into doctoral studies and ultimately establish a career as a leader in immunology research.

column36: Trajectory of brain and cognitive development of children with CHD: neuropsychology and functional connectivity
column37: Congenital heart diseases are cardiac malformations that occur during the intrauterine period and are amongst the most common in infants. It is estimated that 8.23 out of 1000 babies are born with a congenital heart disease. Depending on the malformations' severity, some of the babies have to undergo one or many restorative surgeries in the days following their birth. About 50% of the survivors develop impairments in one or many areas of their functioning (learning skills, speech and language, motor skills, social skills, memory, attention, and executive functions). Several impacts on the quality of life of these children are due to these neurodevelopmental delays, including significant academic, social and behavioral difficulties. My project aims to document the development of brain networks in children with congenital heart diseases. More specifically, I want to compare brain networks of children with congenital heart diseases to those of healthy children at 42 months old and investigate the relationship between brain networks and developmental profiles. In an exploratory way, I will also document the developmental trajectory of the brain networks in children with congenital heart disease, between 4 and 42 months of age. To do so, children with congenital heart disease and healthy children will undergo a developmental evaluation using behavioral tests. We will also measure their functional brain connectivity using near infrared spectroscopy (NIRS). A better comprehension of brain development and its relationship with developmental outcomes will allow a better understanding of the neural substrates of cognitive and motor disabilities in CHD. As a long term goal, this will help to provide more adapted intervention strategies to this pediatric population.

column36: Role des macrophages senescents dans les maladies associees a l'age.
column37: La senescence est un arret permanent de la division cellulaire agissant comme mecanisme anti-tumoral. Les cellules senescentes produisent beaucoup de secretions, appelees <<senescent-associated secretory phenotype>> (SASP). Le SASP comprend beaucoup de secretions solubles (appelees cytokines) pro-inflammatoires. Ainsi, a court terme, le SASP contribue a activer le systeme immunitaire pour eliminer les cellules senescentes, ce qui est benefique. Par contre, a long terme, le SASP provoque une inflammation chronique et une dysfonction tissulaire. Il a ete montre que, dans les modeles de souris, les cellules senescentes s'accumulent avec l'age et que leur elimination pouvait ameliorer la sante des souris vieillissantes et meme diminuer la presentation de maladies associees au vieillissement. Aussi, il a ete montre que les macrophages representent une large portion des cellules senescentes. Ces macrophages senescents ont une forte activite pro-cancer et sont entre autres impliques dans l'atherosclerose. Par ailleurs, les cellules senescentes secretent plus de vesicules extracellulaires (VE) que les cellules non-senescentes, suggerant les que VE sont importantes dans le SASP. Nous voulons donc developper un modele in vitro de macrophages senescents et caracteriser leurs secretions solubles (cytokines) et vesiculaires (VE). De plus, nous voulons etudier l'effet de ces secretions sur d'autres cellules. A plus long terme, ces etudes fourniront des informations essentielles pour mieux eliminer les macrophages senescents, qui ont un fort impact sur le vieillissement et ses maladies reliees, ou a tout le moins pour diminuer l'impact de leurs secretions sur les cellules environnantes et sur l'organisme.

column36: Effects of testosterone replacement therapy on physiological and behavioural parameters among hypogonadal men with type 2 diabetes
column37: The Canadian Diabetes Association estimates that 30% of the adult population in Ontario will have prediabetes or diabetes by 2020. Prospective studies indicate that low testosterone (T) is a significant risk factor for the development of type 2 diabetes (T2D). Further, upwards of 40% of men with T2D meet clinical criteria for hypogonadism. Recent work indicates that testosterone replacement therapy (TRT) in hypogonadal T2D men has many beneficial effects, including decreasing insulin resistance, inflammation, fat mass, and increasing sexual function. Despite many of its positive effects, no studies have investigated the behavioural consequences of TRT among men with T2D. This is particularly problematic in light of basic endocrinology research indicating that T can modulate important behavioural outcomes including aggression, risk-taking, and economic decision-making. The current proposal will systematically assess, for the first time, the effects of TRT on physiological and behaviour processes in hypogonadal men with T2D, enabling health care practitioners and patients to make more fully informed decisions - in consideration of both the health and social benefits/costs - about whether TRT is a good treatment option for T2D.

column36: Les facteurs psychosociaux influencant la pratique d'activite physique chez des survivantes du cancer du sein
column37: La survivance au cancer du sein est consideree comme une maladie chronique necessitant l'adoption de saines habitudes de vie afin de prevenir l'exacerbation des symptomes residuels, la diminution potentielle de la qualite de vie ou alors, la recidive du cancer. Neanmoins, ceci constitue un defi pour les survivantes, car la plupart vivent des difficultes biopsychosociales telle que la fatigue persistante qui constitue une consequence majeure des traitements. column36: Emotional Contagion as a Risk Factor in Inpatient Eating Disorder Treatment Programs
column37: There has been mixed feedback regarding the efficacy of inpatient treatment programs for anorexia nervosa, with patients responding positively to peer support, but also reporting body weight comparison and competition (Colton & Pistrang, 2004). There is thus some concern regarding social contagion within inpatient eating disorder (ED) treatment groups, as a subculture of further disordered eating habits can develop among peers (Vandereycken, 2011). There is a need to examine risk factors in EDinpatient programs. Dispositional emotional contagion could be a measure of risk for social contagion among inpatients, as it measures one's propensity to mimic the emotion of others (Hatfield, Rapson, Le, Decety, & Ickes, 2009). This study hypothesizes that higher dispositional emotional contagion will be correlated with poorer treatment outcomesin ED patients in inpatient programs, but not in outpatient programs. There will two groups recruited for this study. One group of participants will be from an inpatient program, and the second group will be from an outpatient program. Participants must score 20 or higher on the Eating Attitudes Test (EAT-26) to qualify (Garner, Olmsted, Bohr & Garfinkel, 1982). Participants will also complete the Emotional Contagion Scale (ECS), and will be paired across groups based on similar ECS scores (Doherty, 1997). Each week for a period of two months, participants will be issued the EAT-26. The results will be analyzed to determine if there is a statistically significant difference between the change in EAT scores for those in inpatient and outpatient groups, mediated by ECS scores. This study has the potential to better inform individual needs in ED treatment programs within the field of Clinical Psychology.

column37: Gonorrhea is a common sexually transmitted infection, caused by the bacterium Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Prevalence of the infection is rising, and many strains of the pathogen are developing resistance to antibiotics. N. gonorrhoeae infects the mucosal surfaces of the genital tract and nasal pharynx of humans. However, mucosal barriers are never sterile; instead, they are naturally inhabited by a community of non-pathogenic microorganisms, collectively called the microbiota. N. gonorrhoeae must therefore compete with the microbiota during its infection. The purpose of my project is to elucidate the interactions between the genital tract microbiota and N. gonorrhoeae infection. I will use humanized mouse models to study this system, and I will test and compare different strains of N. gonorrhoeae, since different strains of the pathogen can have different characteristics. Over the course of N. gonorrhoeae infection, the genital tracts of the mice will be washed out to collect genetic material from the microbiota. Using high-throughput sequencing techniques, the diversity and relative abundances of the microbiota can be assessed, as can the progress and intensity of the N. gonorrhoeae infection. By examining how the diversity of the genital tract microbiota changes over the course of infection, I can determine if N. gonorrhoeae alters the microbiota to create a more favorable environment for itself. Furthermore, by comparing the responses of mice with a healthy microbiota and those with a depleted one, I will be able to investigate whether the genital tract microbiota confer a protective effect against N. gonorrhoeae infection to the host. This will be the first study to fully characterize the role of the genital tract microbiota in the pathogenesis of N. gonorrhoeae.

column36: Genomic Regulation of Pediatric Age Acceleration: Relevance for Child Mental Health
column37: Epigenetic clocks have been validated as clinically relevant biomarkers with the ability to predict adverse health effects in adults. These clocks use genome methylation information at specific sites in the genome to calculate the epigenetic (biological) age of an individual. Epigenetic age acceleration, which is the difference between an individual's chronological age and biological age, predicts many negative outcomes including psychopathology in adults. Recently, an epigenetic clock specific to children - the pediatric clock - has been developed and shown to be of relevance to child neurodevelopment. Our research group is investigating the effects of environmental and biological influences on pediatric age acceleration and its implications on child development and mental health outcomes. We have found that the early care environment predicts variation in pediatric age acceleration. We aim to identify and assess the functionality of genetic biomarkers associated with epigenetic aging, and to determine how epigenetic age acceleration associates with later child psychopathology. A meta-analysis using 5 cohorts (N=1229) will be used for a genome wide association analysis of pediatric age acceleration and for investigation into psychopathologies using parent report symptom checklists available for all children in these cohorts. Analysis of the pediatric clock and its implications provides a unique opportunity to observe genetic and environmental impacts at the level of the individual. This is a necessary step in the direction of personalized medicine in child and youth mental health.

column36: The role of zDHHC9-mediated protein palmitoylation in activity-induced synaptic strengthening
column37: Intellectual disability (ID) is characterized by limitations in cognitive abilities including learning, reasoning and problem solving. While it is known that ID has a strong hereditary component and is caused by disruptions in proper brain development, our understanding of the genes associated with ID and how disrupting their function leads to pathology is still in its infancy. 'Palmitoylation' is a biochemical process involving the reversible addition of palmitate to proteins. Proper palmitoylation of proteins has been shown to be important for the differentiation and outgrowth of nerve cells (neurons), as well as the development and plasticity of specialized connections between neurons, called 'synapses'. Loss-of-function mutations in one of the enzymes that mediate palmitoylation, zDHHC9, has been identified in 2% of all patients with X-linked intellectual disability (XLID). A high proportion of these patients also exhibit epileptic seizures. Our lab has previously demonstrated that zDHHC9 is exceedingly important for the formation of inhibitory synapses and the plasticity of synaptic connections. My goal is to further our understanding of the role of zDHHC9 by determining all downstream substrates for zDHHC9 as well as determining which substrates are specifically palmitoylated by zDHHC9 following a learning event or increased synaptic activity. Together, we propose that identifying the molecular mechanisms that underlie zDHHC9 function in synapse formation and activity-mediated synaptic plasticity is important in order to understand the changes that lead to disease and for advancement of targeted therapeutic interventions.

column36: Effets des contraceptifs oraux sur l'extinction de la peur : Implications pour le developpement du cerveau
column37: Des la puberte, deux fois plus de femmes que d'hommes souffrent d'un trouble anxieux ou d'un trouble de stress post-traumatique. Ces troubles se caracterisent par des niveaux de peur accrus et une capacite amoindrie a reguler la peur. Des pistes ont suggere que les hormones sexuelles, particulierement l'estrogene, pourraient expliquer cette difference entre les sexes. Accedant au cerveau, ces hormones ont un impact sur les structures liees a la regulation de la peur. Des etudes ont demontre que la regulation de la peur etait defaillante chez les femmes ayant des faibles niveaux d'estrogene et celles prenant des contraceptifs oraux (abolissant les variations du cycle menstruel en maintenant une faible secretion de ces hormones). Or, aucune etude n'a considere le moment de la prise de contraceptifs oraux et leurs effets potentiellement durables. A l'adolescence, puisque 1) la prise de contraceptifs oraux est frequemment initiee, 2) le cerveau n'est pas dument developpe et 3) les hormones sexuelles sont particulierement presentes a ce moment, il est pertinent d'examiner si la prise de contraceptifs oraux pendant le developpement cerebral peut modifier la regulation de la peur a long terme. A l'aide d'un modele de laboratoire valide, nous examinerons les patrons d'apprentissage de la peur et la regulation de celle-ci chez des femmes ayant utilise des contraceptifs oraux a l'adolescence, comparativement a celles en ayant utilise a l'age adulte, celles n'en ayant jamais utilise et aux hommes. Sachant que des millions de femmes utilisent ces contraceptifs, ce projet favorisera la reflexion quant aux lignes directrices en matiere de contraception et pourra soutenir l'importance de creer des methodes d'intervention individualisees chez les femmes souffrant de troubles anxieux.

column36: Genetic Associations with Aortic Stenosis in Non-European Populations
column37: Aortic Stenosis (AS) is a common form of valve disease that leads to heart failure and death. Despite its high prevalence in North America, the only current treatment option for AS is surgery. In recent years, genome-wide association studies have been used to help understand the genetic causes of AS. However, these studies have been restricted exclusively to populations of European ancestry. Without robust replication of findings in non-Europeans, results from these studies will not be broadly applicable. In addition, pathways unique to other ethnicities will remain undiscovered. To close this gap, I propose to conduct genome-wide association studies for AS in Black and Hispanic populations. I will first assess whether genetic variants shown to contribute to AS in European populations have the same effect in these ethnicities. I will then look for novel variants that are specific to Black and Hispanic populations. To further understand my results, I will determine if genetic ancestry helps to explain racial differences in the prevalence of AS. The results from my project will help to extend the benefits of AS research to under-represented populations.

column36: Impact de la modalite de transport sur l'activite physique globale, la participation sociale et le bien-etre
column37: La societe moderne est caracterisee par la presence de l'automobile. De 1978 en 2016, les statistiques de la Societe de l'assurance automobile du Quebec demontraient une augmentation plus importante du volume de vehicules de promenade par rapport a l'augmentation du nombre de titulaire de permis de conduire. L'utilisation de l'automobile est associee a des impacts de sante, tel que la pollution atmospherique, le bruit et les traumatismes associes aux collisions. Un quatrieme element de sante a considerer est celui de l'inactivite physique. Il existe des solutions alternatifs au transport automobile, tel que le transport collectif, le velo et la marche. Comment la modalite de transport principal vers le milieu de travail des individus conditionne les autres deplacements? Quel est l'impact de ce mode de deplacement sur l'activite physique global, sur la participation sociale et sur le bien-etre? Mon projet de recherche tentera d'explorer ces questions a partir de donnees issus du projet de recherche INTERACT. Impliquant quatre villes canadiennes, dont Montreal, le projet INTERACT mesure notamment la geolocalisation, le deplacement et le mode de transport utilise en temps reel de ses participants dans le but, entre autres, d'evaluer l'effet de la modification de l'environnement urbain sur l'activite physique, la participation sociale et le bien-etre. La particularite de mon projet de recherche est qu'il met en relation la globalite de l'activite physique, le bien-etre et la participation selon le mode de transport principal. L'utilisation de telles donnees est possible par le soutien du projet INTERACT.

column36: An Index of the physical and mental health of Indigenous youth and young adults in the Okanagan.
column37: Currently, very little is known about the physical and mental health of Indigenous youth and young adults living in Canada. Studies show that this population suffers from obesity at an increased rate and children of Indigenous people's are also found to experience greater levels of anxiety and other emotional issues. Research has shown that those young people who spend the most amount of time engaging in sedentary activities and screen time have the lowest levels of health-related quality of life and, subsequently, suffer from obesity and obesity-related disorders at increased rates than the general public. For this reason, it is instrumental to further understand how factors such as sedentary activity and screen time affect important health outcomes such as Health-related quality of life, obesity, and psychological well-being. I will look at the inter-relationships between sedentary behavior, physical activity, sleep, weight status, health-related quality of life, and psychological well-being in off-reserve Indigenous youth and young adults by identifying clusters of health behaviors that determine health-related quality of life and psychological well-being. I will also compare cluster membership between off-reserve indigenous 8- 25 year old's with age- and sex-matched Canadian children. We will be working with our local School District, universities, friendship centers, Metis Associations, and youth groups, to recruit 100 Indigenous young people for this cross-sectional study. Anthropometric measures of weight status will be taken. Sleep, sedentary time, and physical activity will be assessed using an accelerometer/inclinometer worn for one week. This study is an important first step in understanding health determinants in the young off-reserve Indigenous population

column36: Investigating a Kinase as a Target for Alzheimer's Disease
column37: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the most common form of dementia, accounting for 60-70 percent of the approximately 50 million dementia cases worldwide, as reported by the World Health Organization. Patients experiencing the neurodegeneration associated with this disease do not have treatment options that interfere with disease progression; current treatments only alleviate symptoms. This project will investigate the protein calcium/calmodulin dependant protein kinase 1 delta (CaMK1D) as a novel target for late-onset Alzheimer's disease (LOAD). Several studies have linked CaMK1D to AD, including genetic studies and studies examining the amount of CaMK1D and specific fragments of CaMK1D in the brains of AD patients. Here, three main hypotheses will be explored. First, that CaMK1D is modified, cut into smaller pieces, and hyperactive during AD. Second, that the hyperactivity of CaMK1D leads to modification of other AD related proteins to resemble their state in AD, and lastly, the use of specific inhibitors for CaMK1D can control the progression of AD type pathology in cell culture. To explore these hypotheses, neuronal cell culture methods that mimic the AD state biochemically will be used as a model. Determination of the state and function of CaMK1D in AD models, as well as its contribution to AD pathways, represents a new strategy for stopping progression of AD.

column36: Awake 2-photon Imaging of an Alzheimer's Disease Rat Model
column37: Alzheimer's Disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disease accounting for the majority of dementia cases. The disease is categorized by accumulation of extracellular amyloid plaques and intracellular neurofibrillary tangles. Symptoms of disease include speech difficulties, memory deficits, and eventual impairments to basic life functions due to widespread neuronal loss. Neurons are the basic functional cells within the brain and require oxygen and glucose from the blood for activity and survival. AD disrupts the delivery of reagents to the brain and this is referred to as defective neurovascular coupling. Most studies have examined neurovascular coupling in mouse models under anesthesia. Confounding those studies is the fact that anesthesia modulates the delivery of blood to the brain. Additionally, mice models do not completely recapitulate symptoms of the disease. An advanced microscopy technique is used to study neurovascular coupling. This technique is a very powerful microscope that can be used to simultaneously monitor neurons activation and changes to the blood vessels near them. Tg-F344-AD is a rat model which recapitulates age-dependent nature of AD exhibiting amyloid plaques and neurofibrillary tangles leading to frank neuronal loss. This study will use Tg-F344-AD rat model to examine neurovascular coupling within a specific region of the brain called medial prefrontal cortex while awake. I hypothesize there will be an age- and disease-dependent decline in neurovascular coupling response. This study will be the first of its kind to examine the medial prefrontal cortex in AD within the context of an awake animal model. It would aid in our understanding of AD without confounding variables such as anesthesia which disrupt normal brain physiology.

column36: Prediction assistee par intelligence artificielle des sequelles des commotions cerebrales du sport depuis la ligne de touche : est-ce que la sciences des donnees sera mise sur la ligne de touche par les protagonistes des sports de contact ?
column37: Au Quebec tout comme aux Etats-Unis, les commotions cerebrales liees a la pratique sportive sont un probleme de sante publique. Au moment de l'accident, les outils de depistage disponibles pour l'equipe d'intervenants medicaux sont bases sur l'observation de symptomes pour justifier le retrait et le retour au jeu d'un athlete. Malgre des annees de perfectionnement, l'approche basee sur les symptomes cliniques post-commotionnels s'avere dangereuse en raison du faux sentiment de securite qu'elle procure. D'ailleurs, les athletes sont plutot enclins a minimiser leurs symptomes afin de retourner rapidement au jeu. Ce programme de recherche se distingue en offrant une alternative se basant sur des parametres objectifs et quantifiables de l'integrite cerebrale par l'entremise de techniques de neuroimagerie avancee et des proprietes biomecaniques des coups portes a la tete. L'objectif de cette etude est de modeliser, pour la premiere fois, les modifications de l'integrite du cerveau engendrees par l'application de forces portees a la tete lors d'un contact durant un match chez des joueurs de football universitaires. Ultimement, cette modelisation basee sur l'intelligence artificielle fournira une analyse en temps reel du risque d'un athlete de presenter des lesions cerebrales a la suite d'un coup a la tete en s'appuyant sur les forces d'acceleration enregistrees a partir du casque. Cette modelisation permettra que la prise de decision quant au retrait du jeu d'un joueur soit basee sur des donnees objectives de risque de dommage au cerveau, plutot que sur des symptomes subjectifs, auto-rapportes par l'athlete.

column36: Trouble disruptif avec dysregulation emotionnelle, depression, desespoir, suicidalite et traits borderline chez des adolescents en milieu clinique
column37: Le DSM-5 presente un nouveau diagnostic chez l'enfant et l'adolescent?; le trouble disruptif avec dysregulation emotionnelle (TDDE). Il se caracterise par de l'irritabilite chronique, entrainant plusieurs crises de colere par semaine. Althoff (2016), indique que les adolescents ayant un TDDE rapportent plus d'ideations et de comportements suicidaires que les jeunes ayant une autre psychopathologie. De plus, le TDDE est associe a un risque eleve de trouble depressif au debut de l'age adulte (Brotman et al., 2006). L'impulsivite liee a la colere, la suicidalite et la gestion difficile de l'humeur sont trois elements qui rejoignent le trouble de personnalite borderline. Toutefois, a notre connaissance, aucune recherche ne fait encore le lien entre le TDDE et les traits borderline. Afin de faciliter l'identification du TDDE, Breton, Bergeron et Labelle (2011) ont construit une echelle de depistage qui a ete distribuee a Montreal dans diverses cliniques. Aussi, plusieurs recherches ont propose des traitements psychologiques pour le TDDE. Toutefois, il n'existe pas de consensus a ce niveau. Ce projet vise a determiner dans quelle mesure le TDDE est lie a la depression, au desespoir, a la suicidalite et aux traits borderline et a recenser les differents traitements afin de determiner les meilleures pratiques. Les 192 participants ages de 12 a 15 ans ont complete plusieurs instruments psychometriques mesurant toutes les variables a l'etude. Des analyses bivariees permettront d'observer la force du lien entre le TDDE et les autres concepts. Une revue systematique portera sur les traitements psychologiques proposes pour le TDDE. Ainsi, reconnaitre et definir le TDDE a l'adolescence permettra de favoriser la prevention du suicide et de pathologies ayant une incidence a vie.

column36: Is Delirium Associated with Depression and Anxiety in Caregivers of the Critically Ill?
column37: Family caregivers are important partners during and after a patient's stay in the intensive care unit (ICU). Caregivers who visit patients in the ICU may witness delirium, a medical state of confusion that impacts 45-87% of ICU patients. Seeing delirium can be very distressing; for example, caregivers who witnessed delirium in palliative care patients were 12 times more likely to have symptoms of anxiety compared to caregivers who had not. It is important to understand how delirium plays a role in caregiver depression and anxiety, and whether caregivers continue to face these burdens after the patient has returned home. This project is a prospective cohort study nested within a randomized controlled trial that is recruiting caregivers of patients in Foothills Medical Centre medical-surgical ICU (Calgary, Alberta) and measures symptoms of depression, anxiety, and delirium using the Patient Health Questionnaire 9-Item (PHQ-9), Generalized Anxiety Disorder 7-Item (GAD-7), and the Intensive Care Delirium Screening Checklist (ICDSC), respectively. We aim to see how the number of new and existing cases of depression and anxiety in ICU caregivers compares to the general population. We will also see if caregivers of patients with delirium are more likely to have depression and anxiety. Caregiver depression and anxiety will be measured for a maximum of 5 ICU-days and at 3- and 6-months after the patient leaves the ICU to see if these symptoms continue. This study will be the first to evaluate patient delirium and caregiver depression and anxiety in an ICU setting. With Canada's aging population and projected 80% increase in ICU admissions by 2026, it is crucial that we address delirium as a factor that may significantly impact the mental health in Canadian ICU caregivers.

column36: Stress des enfants durant la transition du prescolaire au scolaire : Le role du cortisol dans le developpement des troubles de sante mentale
column37: Sachant que 50% des maladies mentales apparaissent avant l'age de 14 ans, il est important d'identifier un mecanisme precoce de vulnerabilite. D'ailleurs, il a ete observe que la sante mentale pouvait etre associee a une exposition elevee ou prolongee au stress mesure par l'hormone cortisol. Par ailleurs, il a ete demontre que la transition du prescolaire au scolaire, consideree comme un stresseur social universel, est associee a une augmentation du niveau de cortisol, malgre des differences individuelles importantes. Des recherches ont egalement demontre un lien entre le cortisol et les troubles interiorises ainsi qu'entre le cortisol et un temperament inhibe. Ce projet de recherche aura donc 3 objectifs : (a) dresser un patron de la reaction cortisolaire lors de la transition du prescolaire au scolaire; (b) observer si des reactions cortisolaires atypiques sont liees a des difficultes de sante mentale et si ce lien differe selon le sexe; (c) identifier les facteurs de vulnerabilite a des reactions cortisolaires atypiques. Plus particulierement, il sera determine, selon differents patrons de reactions, si des reactions cortisolaires atypiques sont liees a des troubles interiorises et dans quelle mesure le temperament inhibe sera moderateur de ces reactions. Pour ce faire, des donnees d'un projet en cours de collecte suivant environ 400 enfants de la prematernelle a la 2e annee du primaire seront utilisees. En bref, cette etude permettra de mieux comprendre l'experience et l'ampleur de la reaction de stress des enfants lors de la transition scolaire ainsi que son implication fonctionnelle. Ceci facilitera alors le developpement d'outils de depistage ou de prevention precoce, car l'entree scolaire constitue un moment privilegie pour le depistage systematique precoce.

column36: Natural Antisense Transcripts and Their Potential as Toxoplasmosis Drug Targets
column37: Toxoplasma gondii is a parasitic protozoan that causes Toxoplasmosis, a disease that affects more than half of the world's population and is a leading cause of death in immunocompromised humans. Despite the prevalence and medical significance of Toxoplasmosis, there is currently no cure for this disease. To develop effective treatments for Toxoplasmosis, biomolecules involved in cellular processes of T. gondii often serve as good targets for drug discoveries. A gene important for T. gondii growth and virulence, known as the ubiquitin-like protease 1 (Ulp1), was found to be controlled by a transcription unit on the opposite strand referred to as the Ulp1-Natural Antisense Transcript (Ulp1-NAT). To examine whether Ulp1-NAT affects T. gondii growth and virulence by regulating Ulp1, CRISPR Intereference (CRISPRi) is used for analysis along with replication and plaque assays. By studying how the Ulp1-NAT controls Ulp1 and its resulting impact on parasite fitness, efficacious drugs for treating Toxoplasmosis can be created and put an end to this global threat.

column36: Is natural folate as effective as synthetic folic acid in increasing plasma and red blood cell folate concentrations during pregnancy? A proof-of-concept pilot study
column37: Adequate folate status in early pregnancy is associated with prevention of neural tube defects (NTD). For this reason, Health Canada recommends pregnant women consume 0.4-1 mg/day of folic acid. Folic acid is a synthetic, man-made source of folate. A recently developed form of natural folate (Metafolin) is gaining popularity in Canada. It is being used increasingly in prenatal multivitamins, but has never been evaluated in pregnancy. Natural folate and folic acid are metabolized differently. Natural folate can enter circulation directly, whereas folic acid must be converted to folate through a series of steps. Recent evidence suggests that humans cannot convert such large doses of folic acid. In amounts as low as 0.2 mg/day, there is a build-up of unmetabolized folic acid in the blood, which has been associated with acceleration of some cancers and altered DNA development. Thus, natural folate may be safer for pregnant women and their babies than synthetic folic acid. We aim to test whether supplementation with natural folate can increase blood folate levels to at least 906nmol/L, a level associated with a very low risk of NTDs. Second, we aim to test if supplementation with natural folate results in lower unmetabolized folic acid levels, as compared to synthetic folic acid. We will randomize 60 healthy pregnant women to 0.6 mg folic acid or natural folate for 16 weeks. We will initiate the trial in later pregnancy, after neural tube closure, to reduce the risk of harm should the natural folate prove less effective. We will measure levels of serum folate, red blood cell folate, and unmetabolized folic acid. This proof-of-concept trial is the first step in determining the safest and most effective form of folate supplements for Canadian women and their babies.

column36: The Efficacy of Postnatal Choline Supplementation on Reversing Deficits in Hippocampal Plasticity Induced by Prenatal Ethanol Exposure
column37: Consuming alcohol during pregnancy causes a range of lifelong effects on the offspring, known as Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorders (FASD). Recent research has explored supplementing the essential nutrient choline to mitigate the associated cognitive deficits. These studies have seen promising results when measuring behavioural outcomes in both animal studies of prenatal ethanol exposure (PNEE) and in clinical trials. However, little is understood of the mechanisms behind this treatment. This study will use a rodent model of FASD to elucidate changes within the hippocampus, an area of the brain vital to memory consolidation. Memories are formed from the strengthening of neuronal synapses, a process known as long term potentiation (LTP). LTP is modulated by cholinergic inputs, acetylcholine producing neurons, and alteration of these circuits may be one mechanism in which choline rescues cognitive impairments. Offspring will be exposed to ethanol throughout the gestational period, with 35.5% of the caloric intake derived from ethanol. Choline treatment will begin on postnatal day 10. Hippocampal-dependent behavioural tasks will validate that choline rescues memory deficits in this model of PNEE. Electrophysiological recordings in the dentate gyrus of the hippocampus will elucidate changes on a molecular level, specifically to determine if choline enhances LTP in PNEE animals. Additionally, pharmaceutical agents that block cholinergic receptors or stimulate their activity will confirm that the modulation of LTP is dependent on local changes in choline activity. Together, these experiments will further define the mechanisms behind postnatal choline supplementation and provide molecular evidence for the rescuing of cognitive impairments in this potential treatment of FASD.

column36: Network Analysis for Modeling Multimorbidity in Administrative Data
column37: Multimorbidity, the presence of two or more chronic medical conditions, results in poorer health outcomes, including lower quality of life, for those that experience it. Today, more people are living with multimorbidity than ever because of an aging population and increasing rates of certain chronic diseases and their risk factors, like obesity. This makes reducing and managing multimorbidity a very important task for Canadians. In addition to improving quality of life, reducing multimorbidity will considerably reduce government spending on healthcare services. This project will look at the types of chronic conditions that cluster together, to better understand profiles of multimorbidity in the population. In order to do this, we will use data for the entire population that is found in administrative health records (hospital, physician, and prescription records) as well as electronic medical records. The detailed information found in these administrative data will be analyzed using computer rules that identify patterns of chronic conditions in the population. We will experiment with and evaluate different computing techniques for constructing these disease networks. We will also compare the results obtained from administrative data alone to when electronic medical records are incorporated. After completing this research, we will summarize these comparisons so that other researchers could learn from our work. The conclusions we arrive at will lead to recommendations about methods to measure multimorbidity and will guide future multimorbidity research. This research will help to inform disease prevention and management actions, which can lead to cost savings for the Canadian healthcare system and improve the lives of those living with multiple chronic conditions.

column36: L'adaptation saccadique chez les personnes agees saines et ayant une degenerescence maculaire liee a l'age
column37: La degenerescence maculaire liee a l'age (DMLA) est grandement handicapante: elle entraine habituellement une perte de la vision centrale, ne laissant intacte que la vision peripherique. Jusqu'a ce jour, il n'existe aucun traitement contre la maladie et les patients doivent s'y adapter en utilisant un point de fixation attentionnel en peripherie, une habitude extremement difficile a implanter qui peut demander des annees de travail. Pourtant, les systemes des mouvements oculaires et de l'attention, enormement sollicites dans la vision, sont connus pour etre particulierement plastiques et rapides a entrainer. Les patients ayant la DMLA pourraient grandement beneficier d'un deplacement efficace de leur attention en peripherie, en effectuant des mouvements oculaires adaptes a leur perte de vision. Par ailleurs, il est possible d'entrainer nos saccades, automatiques, a se modifier: c'est l'adaptation saccadique. Cette methode produit des effets en une periode tres courte, effets qui se maintiennent pourtant a long terme. A ce jour, nous ignorons s'il est possible, en l'absence de vision centrale, d'augmenter l'efficacite du traitement visuel par l'adaptation saccadique. En entrainant la modification des saccades en presence d'une tache de discrimination visuelle en peripherie, sans vision centrale, la presente etude pourra explorer cette possibilite. Des personnes agees saines, pour lesquelles la perte de vision centrale sera simulee, et des personnes ayant la DMLA participeront au programme d'entrainement. Si des changements positifs s'observent, cette etude permettra d'etablir des programmes d'intervention efficaces pour ameliorer le traitement visuel chez les patients ayant la DMLA, ce qui aurait un impact majeur sur leur fonctionnement quotidien et leur qualite de vie.
